$comment: Phase 787 — the pinned prover for every model under proofs/ (RemotingDecode.fst, and since Phase 790 DisclosureFold.fst; check.ps1 carries the module list).
F* releases WEEKLY (five releases in the four weeks to 2026-09-13), and a proof is a
claim about a specific prover: an unpinned toolchain would silently change what the
green tick means, and proof hints no longer exist to stabilise it (--record_hints and
--use_hints were removed from F*), so reproducibility rests on this pin, on --quake,
and on the margin in z3rlimit. The release bundles Z3, so the pin covers the solver too
— three of them, and z3version names which one is used.
The hash is over the downloaded archive; proofs/check.ps1 verifies it before extracting
and refuses to proceed on a mismatch.
Phase 792 adds ModelInput.fst, the model-input admissibility theorem. It needed no flag
change either: the `extract` set below still carries only --codegen FSharp, and check.ps1
appends --extract <module> per entry of its own module list. A model that ever DID need a
flag of its own would take a per-module override here rather than widening this set.

linux-x64.$comment: Declared but NOT hash-pinned: nothing in this repo has run the proof leg on Linux, and an unverified hash recorded as if it were verified is worse than an absent one. check.ps1 refuses a platform whose sha256 is empty and says why. The CI job runs windows-latest for this reason.

flags.$comment: --z3rlimit 60 against modules whose slowest query finishes well inside the default is a deliberate MARGIN, not a requirement: with hints gone, the thing that makes a check flaky is a query landing near the limit on a slower machine, and headroom is the cheapest defence available. `extract` carries no `--extract <module>`: check.ps1 appends one per module from its list, so a second model did not need a second flag set (Phase 790).
